hyps.why: Turning a missing edge into a conv reconnects a disconnected output (row 91, +78) while swapping an existing op for a conv gives small gains.
Filling an empty edge into the output node restores an input-to-output path (row 92, +77), far more than refining an existing edge.
Adding a conv where there was no edge reconnects the output node (row 93, +76) whereas rows with an existing edge 5 change little.
Replacing a missing edge with a skip restores the signal path to the output (row 95, +78; row 56, +3 to +12) versus replacing an existing op.
A skip on an empty edge 3 reconnects input to output (row 96, +74; row 54 positive) and is a bigger gain than replacing a conv.
Skip on an empty final edge restores a path to the output node (row 94, +79) whereas it is neutral to harmful when edge 5 already has an op.
With edge 5 absent, edge 3 is more likely the sole route into the output, so adding a conv there matters much more (row 91 vs rows 52, 61).
When edge 5 is absent, edge 4 is a critical route to the output, so a conv there helps far more (row 92 +77, row 33 +6 to +16 vs rows 53 and 68).
With edge 3 empty, upgrading edge 5 can reconnect or strengthen the only route to the output (row 93, +76) versus small gains when edge 3 is populated.
Removing edge 5 when edge 4 is already absent cuts the last path into the output (row 57, -76) while other parents lose only a few points.
